subject: English
passage: One challenge faced by literary translators, as essayist Satoshi Tang observes, is that different languages carve up the realm of emotion in different ways. Many translators rely on finding a single word in the target language that matches a feeling named in the source. However, languages do not all draw the same boundaries around a feeling; for instance, Portuguese has the word saudade for a bittersweet longing, while German uses Sehnsucht for a related but distinct yearning. Some languages also blend emotional states with moral or social judgments in a single term. This variation makes it difficult for translators to render emotional nuance faithfully across traditions.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To compare the emotional vocabularies of two different languages.
choices.B: To explain why translators are drawn to working with literary texts.
choices.C: To illustrate a problem faced by literary translators.
choices.D: To object to an approach that some translators use when rendering emotion words.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer. The text describes a challenge faced by literary translators: different languages carve up emotional experience differently. It then illustrates this problem with examples (Portuguese saudade, German Sehnsucht) and explains that this variation makes it difficult for translators to render emotional nuance faithfully across traditions.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. The text neutrally describes the different ways languages categorize emotion without objecting to any approach translators take.
